catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class carries one communication/msg/ActuatorCmds publication with its five per-actuator arrays. cap.motion.joint_position.v1 carries only joint positions and would drop kp, kd, vel and torque, while its reached field cannot be observed from a rosbridge publication. The extension keeps the native message arrays and the fixed 12-name MJCF order.

No catalogue class carries the communication/srv/SimulationReset request (header, base_pose, joint_state) and its is_success response. cap.world.reset.v1 takes scenario and seed and requires observation plus seed in its output, which this service does not provide; cap.device.configure.v1 is a state write, not an effectful simulated-world reset.

No catalogue class is an input-free acknowledged simulation reset that can serve as a declared safe-state action. cap.world.reset.v1 takes scenario/seed and returns observation/seed; the fixed-input form of the upstream reset service is the only acknowledged route that zeroes the cached actuator commands, so it is declared as an extension safe-state action.

No catalogue class carries a sensor_msgs/msg/JointState sample. cap.sensing.read.v1 is a named-channel read with an open values object and cannot bind a fixed ROS subscription or preserve the joint name/position/velocity/effort arrays in message order; cap.sensing.imu.v1 is IMU-specific. The extension preserves the native message fields.

notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The last gate run printed digest sha256:e2cfdd7cfd54388940aead443fe40dfadf5b8d630a805eb8259f99b9addab840 with failed=[], G1-G9 pass and no warnings. This package is model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run ros-wave-c-131) and unreviewed: driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null. No human reviewed or tested anything, no hardware was attached, and no live ROS 2 graph, rosbridge endpoint, MuJoCo execution or physical Spot run is claimed.

SHAPE AND SCOPE: the card is family:ros with RosDriver, and the pinned clone really is a ROS 2 runtime: simulation/mujoco/src/MuJoCoMessageHandler.cpp creates the relative sim_reset service (communication/srv/SimulationReset, lines 13-16), the relative actuators_cmds subscription (communication/msg/ActuatorCmds, lines 47-51) and the relative joint_states publisher (sensor_msgs/msg/JointState, lines 21-22) under name_prefix simulation/ (lines 8-9). The package therefore stays a configuration-only RosDriver with ros_version 2; no Python native class exists and no native.py is used. The primary control is one x-cap actuator publication on /simulation/actuators_cmds with the 12 actuator names fixed to the MJCF order (spot_mini.xml:230-243) and caller-supplied kp, pos, kd, vel and torque arrays of 12; the node evaluates kp*(pos-qpos)+kd*(vel-qvel)+torque and clamps data.ctrl to [-100,100] (main.cc:261-286). A publication receipt reports published=true and confirmed=false only. The resource snapshot is the live joint_positions array from /simulation/joint_states; an explicit x-cap read of the same topic returns frame, names, positions, velocities and efforts (MuJoCoMessageHandler.cpp:203-222). The acknowledged /simulation/sim_reset action carries the fixed model frame_id spot, optional base pose fields and optional 12 joint positions; its callback calls mj_resetData, writes qpos, zeroes cached commands and returns is_success (lines 74-121).

RISK AND SAFE STATE: the device is simulated but the actuator command drives a legged mobile base, so risk is R2 rather than the card floor R0. The runtime latches in software and the native e-stop binding is the fixed-input /simulation/sim_reset service; the same fixed binding is safety_bindings.reset and the input-free x-cap.mindspaceinc.safe_reset.v1 action is safe_state=True. The reset is an acknowledged simulated state reset: it restores mj_resetData defaults plus the fixed base pose (0,0,0.7 identity), zeroes every cached actuator command and leaves the MuJoCo physics loop running. It is not a pause, not a physical emergency stop and it does not guarantee that the simulated bodies remain still. Normal invocation of the safe-state action does not engage the latch. mhs.resource.read remains permitted while latched; the extension joint_states read action remains latched after an e-stop because an extension read verb is not a catalogue-confirmed read exemption. No estop_physical_ref is claimed and no hardware backend is declared.

LIMITS: only the torque feed-forward array declares a sourced bound, -100..100 N.m, from the same apply_ctrl clamp line (main.cc:284-285); every element of the array is checked. The kp, pos, kd and vel arrays have no source-backed envelope in the clone, so no bound was invented for them. The action's 12-element lengths are the model's 12 actuators (spot_mini.xml:230-243); they are declared structural lengths, not Limits. No site-limits.example.json is needed because no Limit.operator_required path is declared.

FAKE AND FIDELITY: fake.py is a ROS-free analytic rosbridge contract stand-in, not a recording of captured traffic and not the upstream simulation executable. It answers advertise/publish on the command topic, a fresh joint_states subscription and the acknowledged reset service, including negative paths for a rejected application response, a transport failure and a malformed response. It is F0 with analytic engine, determinism none, timestep 0 ms, realtime factor 0, reset partial and no snapshot/restore; the driver's gaps list every difference. Its 12 joint entries and all numeric samples are placeholders. It runs no MuJoCo physics, PD law, contact or timers; it only nudges its placeholder joint-position sample by a fixed small factor of the PD expression so a publication has an observable, input-dependent contract effect. The real node publishes joint states from a 1 ms timer and applies the command in its own physics loop, neither of which the fake reproduces. The 0.0005 s model timestep, the 0.2 s stale-command zeroing and the 1/2/2.5/20/100 ms timers are source facts, not fake behavior.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds 13 cases: fixed-order publication and recorded arrays; sourced torque-envelope refusal through the strict server; fresh joint-state read; reset updates the placeholder base pose; rejected reset application; failed reset transport; malformed joint-state sample; failed application, failed transport and malformed reset through the actual driver.estop() path; latched command refusal after a completed e-stop; the input-free safe-state action that does not latch and is followed by an accepted command; and the extension observation refused while latched while the resource read remains available. All pass. The fake's negative-path switches are test data, not facts.

NOT COVERED: the MuJoCo engine and its physics/contacts; the live ROS 2 graph, rosbridge, launch file and colcon build; the /simulation/imu_data and /simulation/odom publishers; the /simulation/touch_sensor publisher; and the /simulation/depth_image and /simulation/rgb_image topics, whose callback constructs a CvImage but publishes neither (MuJoCoMessageHandler.cpp:224-238). Images are not the primary interface of this simulator and the package does not substitute metadata for them. The README lists the four published topics (README.md:44-53), but only joint_states is exposed. The upstream install needs a ROS 2 Humble workspace and colcon build --symlink-install (README.md:17-42); neither was installed or run. The upstream licence is NOASSERTION and publish_review is required; this pass is not a publication or licence decision. The clone at commit 1e07b87745ab623dab7ab79c4fbc61e62e4e829e was read only and git status --porcelain is empty. check-report.json is the gate's own report from the last run.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked endpoints, types, message fields, the torque Limit (main.cc:284-285), all 19 facts, the fake and the stop. The sim_reset stop holds as a simulated reset: under the sim mutex, before answering, it calls mj_resetData and zeroes the cached commands apply_ctrl reads (MuJoCoMessageHandler.cpp:74-121). But safe_state omitted that the robot is teleported to the start pose and, physics running, falls limp; one fact claimed physics continues, which the callback cannot show; the image fact cited lines outside its range. Reviewer rewrote safe_state and the docstring, narrowed both facts, added two facts (startup sleep loop, PhysicsLoop) and two gaps (two teleporting reset calls per e-stop; unbounded PD inputs) (driver.py), gave the fake's JointState a ROS 2 stamp (fake.py), updated facts.md, regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; gate and collect.py --strict pass, digest unchanged. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: The e-stop teleports the simulated Spot to (0, 0, 0.7) with zero commands; physics keeps running, so it drops and lies limp (kd 1.0 after 0.2 s); any actuators_cmds client re-commands it. Reset-as-stop accepted because it clears the commanded state. Simulation only.
